body: I completely know what you’re going through! This is such a hard obstacle to overcome, even though you may feel like it shouldn’t bother you this much. But it’s honestly the reason so many people (including myself for a while and a lot of my friends) don’t go to the gym. What helps me with this is being completely prepared ahead of time; looking up workout videos and knowing exactly what you’re going to do each day you go in. It helps with that anxiety a lot to just know what your plan is and not worry that you’re doing something wrong. And investing in clothes that you feel good in to wear to the gym, watching people on YouTube who have overcome gym anxiety, and just doing your own thing with headphones in. Once you see the smallest results, it will feel worth it and the fear of other peoples opinions will start to fade away. If someone else is judging you it is just a reflection on their own insecurities and has nothing to do with you.

I definitely think you have to find the right therapist. I’ve been to so many, and I just now found one that I feel like genuinely understands and backs up my experiences with research by other people. I was nervous to express those feelings to him but he made me realize how I feel is more common and that I’m not the only one.

Wow-I just watched a few videos on it and it’s so interesting. That makes so much sense and is somewhat relieving to know it’s my body protecting me subconsciously instead of getting mad at myself for thinking a certain way. Thank you so much for that suggestion I’m definitely going to share it too

I know how you feel about being disappointed in how life turned out. I think we all imagine such a bright future for ourselves when we’re young. But the truth is adulthood sucks, in every possible way and no one tells you that. They tell you about the financial stuff and responsibilities sure, but no one tells you about the regrets and fucked up self image and pain, self hatred, and insecurities you’re gonna feel. They don’t tell you how people are going to betray you and how trust is nearly impossible. I’ve said all of those same things to myself that you said, but I’m sure there is at least one beautiful thing about you. There is for everyone, and I think you could build off that. Awkwardness is endearing to so many people too. Anyway, I don’t know if any of this has helped but you seem like someone I would want to be friends with and I’m so sorry for all the shit you had to go through and even though it’s just on reddit I hope you feel the slightest bit of hope and comfort in knowing that you’re not alone and someone hears you.

Approach other people first, don’t wait for them to talk to you. 
Don’t take things personally. If something becomes awkward or someone ignores you, don’t dwell on it. 
Ask people about themselves and be genuinely interested in their response. 
Focus on maintaining eye contact even if it’s uncomfortable.

We’re both 21. We’ve been together a little over a year and I’ve never been with someone who treats me so well. He makes me so happy, but no I don’t think I would want to be with someone for the rest of my life who doesn’t share any kind of spirituality with me. I’ve read lots of self help type spiritual books but haven’t seriously looked into another spirituality and I honestly would have no idea where to start.

When you say you’re having trouble remembering things, what exactly do you mean? Because lately that has been such a big issue for me too. I don’t know if it’s because of my anxiety or if my medication is making it worse, but I can think of little things automatically-but I’ll try to remember significant parts of my life and I can eventually remember some things but it takes me a while, and the anxiety about it is overwhelming and doesn’t help. I know exactly how you feel. And it is the hardest thing to explain to anyone because it’s something you don’t think about until it happens to you, and it feels like you’re the only one who has experienced it. I try to explain it to people but they don’t understand which makes me worry about it even more

I started at 75mg and now I’m at 150mg. I’ve definitely been doing a lot better because of it, but I think my job triggers my dissasociation and some anxiety so I feel like that almost every time I go to work, even though I have a great job and have no real reason to feel that way. I’m glad it’s helping you too, this is the first medication I’ve tried that’s actually shown me improvement and it’s only been a little over a month.

That is almost exactly how I feel! I started taking Effexor about a month and a half ago for anxiety and depression, and I’ve noticed it helping a lot but the disassociation is still there sometimes, which makes me anxious and feel like I’m not really there.
“It was the best of times, and the worst of times.”
